Subject: Encryption / KMS follow-up

Hi Sarah / Tom,

Thanks again for taking the call earlier — great to meet the Ensight team. Quick recap and next steps on the encryption and key-management topics we covered: 

- Scope / ask: Ensight needs customer-managed key support for PII workloads, ability to host keys in your AWS account, strict logging/retention controls (auditability of key usage), and data residency in the US.
- In-transit: All Redwood-hosted endpoints use TLS 1.2+ (TLS 1.3 available). For Dedicated and Private deployments we support mTLS for client auth.
- At-rest: We use envelope encryption by default. Data encrypted at rest using service-managed keys unless customer provides a key (BYOK/CMEK).
- Customer-managed keys: Options we discussed:
  - Hosted with BYOK (CMEK) where customer manages keys in their cloud KMS (AWS KMS/GCP KMS/Azure Key Vault) and we perform cross-account usage via a limited IAM role. Keys never leave the customer's KMS.
  - Dedicated/Private: Option to deploy in your VPC with keys in your account or integrate with an on-prem HSM for full control (FIPS 140-2/3 HSM available for Private deployments).
- Audit & logging: We can export KMS usage events and provide per-request metadata (timestamp, request id, model endpoint, key id) for audit. Log retention is configurable for enterprise customers.
- PII handling: We can apply configurable redaction for debug logs, avoid plaintext persistence, and support shortened retention windows for PII-specific logs.

Attachments: redwood-kms-overview.pdf (high level), encryption-diagram.png. I've also attached a draft SOW for scope/next steps.

Next steps / asks:
1) Can you confirm the key location preference (your AWS account preferred?) and minimum retention period for audit logs?
2) Would you like a technical deep-dive with our solutions engineering (Dev Patel) to walk through the BYOK integration and logs?

Suggested time: Wed 11/25 10:00 AM PT (Dev included). If that works I will send a calendar invite.

Thanks —
Marissa

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications on our side: 

- Key location: Yes — we prefer keys to be in our AWS account (we run in us-west-2).
- Log retention: We have a regulatory requirement to retain audit logs for 7 years. For operational logs (non-audit) we can do shorter retention, but audit records of key usage must be preserved.
- Plaintext persistence: We cannot tolerate any long-term plaintext persistence of PII. If you need temporary plaintext for processing, it must be ephemeral and not written to disk or logs.
- Key rotation / exportability: We rotate keys annually and need to ensure rotation is supported without service disruption. We do not allow key material export.
- Audit detail: Can you provide an example of the per-request audit record you can provide? Specifically we need to see if the record includes the resource accessed, timestamp, requesting principal, and the operation type (encrypt/decrypt).

Tom and I are available for a tech call — Wed 11/25 10:00 AM PT works for us. Please include Dev Patel. Can you also share SOC 2 and any relevant security docs ahead of the call?

Best,
Sarah

Thanks Sarah — this is helpful. Short answers and what we'll bring to the deep-dive: 

- Keys in customer account: Supported. For hosted BYOK we set up a limited cross-account IAM role in your AWS account that allows Redwood to call the KMS GenerateDataKey / Decrypt APIs only for the specific key alias. Key material never leaves your KMS. We can walk through the exact IAM policy during the call.
- Key rotation: Supported via KMS key versions and envelope keys. Rotation is handled by creating new data key versions; we support zero-downtime rotation by keeping prior key versions available for decryption of existing ciphertexts. No key material export is required or permitted.
- Audit records: We can provide the following per-request fields in an audit export (sample): timestamp, request_id, endpoint, model_name, operation_type (encrypt/decrypt), key_id (customer alias), requester_identity (redwood-service-account), request_ip, and correlation_id. We'll bring a sample JSON record to the call.
- Plaintext persistence: Our service is designed to avoid writing plaintext PII to disk for inference workloads. Any transient plaintext used for processing is kept in-memory and zeroed after use; debug logs strip PII by default unless explicitly enabled.
- Retention: For hosted customers the default audit/log retention is 90 days, but for enterprise deals we support extended retention with managed export to your S3/secure archive (we can commit to 7-year retention in the SOW and outline costs).
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ for hosted; mTLS available for Dedicated and Private. We can enable mutual TLS with client certs stored in your PKI if desired.

Attachments: updated SOW-draft.docx with retention and KMS integration options, plus a small encryption-diagram.png that shows envelope flow.

Proposed deep-dive: Wed 11/25 10:00 AM PT — Dev, could you join to cover the integration details and IAM policy?

I'll also upload SOC 2 and security overview to the HubSpot file section before the call and share the link.
